title: X-Frame-Options vs CSP frame-ancestors: protecting against clickjacking (with a passive check)
summary:
Clickjacking is the attack where a malicious site loads your page in a transparent iframe and tricks the victim into clicking buttons they believe belong to the attacker. Two mechanisms stop it — and one of them is being deprecated.



Mechanism
How it works
Status




X-Frame-Options: DENY / SAMEORIGIN
Header: browser refuses to frame the page
Legacy, well supported


CSP frame-ancestors
CSP directive: frame-ancestors 'none' / 'self' / allowlist
Modern, more flexible



X-Frame-Options: ALLOWAL
